title: Velocity
subject: Physics

English.simple_explanation: Velocity is speed together with the direction of travel.
English.detailed_explanation: Speed tells you only how fast something is moving. Velocity tells you how fast and in which direction, so 20 km/h north and 20 km/h south are the same speed but different velocities. Quantities that carry a direction like this are called vectors, while speed is a scalar. Because direction is part of velocity, an object that only turns, without speeding up or slowing down, has still changed its velocity.
English.everyday_example: Two buses may both travel at 40 km/h, but if one is heading towards the market and the other away from it, their velocities are different.

local_example.text: Describing a boat as moving at 10 km/h towards the shore states a velocity, because it gives both the speed and the direction.
local_example.appropriate_usage: Use as a general local-context draft only until reviewed; do not present it as a claim about a specific boat, route, or occupation.

common_misconceptions: Speed and velocity mean exactly the same thing.
An object moving at a constant speed must also have a constant velocity.

observe_around_you.invitation: You need an open space where you can walk in a loop — a yard, a field, a courtyard.
observe_around_you.what_to_do: Walk all the way around the edge and return to exactly where you started. Count your steps as you go.
observe_around_you.what_to_notice: You walked a long way. But your distance from the starting point is now zero. Both of those are true at once.
observe_around_you.concept_link: Speed uses the path you covered; velocity uses displacement, which is the straight line from start to finish and includes direction. A closed loop has zero displacement, so your average velocity was zero no matter how far you walked.
needs: an open space to walk a loop

think_question: Two cars both show 50 km/h on the speedometer, but they are driving in opposite directions. Do they have the same speed? Do they have the same velocity?

misconception_keywords: speed and velocity are the same
reasoning_guide.correct_feedback: Good reasoning: same speed, different velocity, because velocity carries the direction too.
reasoning_guide.partial_feedback: You have the speed part. Now say what the opposite directions do to the velocity.
reasoning_guide.misconception_feedback: Speed and velocity are not the same. Velocity includes direction, so compare the directions here.

challenge.question: Write down the velocity of a bus travelling at 45 km/h towards the north, then explain which part of your answer makes it a velocity rather than a speed.
challenge.hint: A velocity must state a direction as well as a number.
progressive_hints: A velocity must state a direction as well as a number.
Write the value and unit first, then the direction after it.
Point out in your explanation which word is the direction.
challenge.solution: The velocity is 45 km/h towards the north. It is a velocity rather than a speed because it states the direction, 'towards the north', as well as how fast the bus travels.

quiz_questions.question: Which of these describes a velocity rather than only a speed?
quiz_questions.explanation: Only this option gives a direction as well as a magnitude, which is what makes it a velocity.
quiz_questions.hint: Look for the option that tells you which way the object is going.
progressive_hints: Look for the option that tells you which way the object is going.
Three options give only a number and a unit. One adds a direction.
